column3: Consider the pressing urgency of the biodiversity and climate crises, together with the longevity of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. Actions that prevent or reduce emissions or enhance removals, while protecting or restoring biodiversity, that have an immediate, ongoing and permanent effect are more valuable than those with results that materialize temporarily or only over a longer time frame. Avoid the trap of prioritizing speed over resilience (see “permanence and long-term impacts” below). This climate urgency never justifies shortening, rushing, or circumventing consultation processes with indigenous peoples and local communities.

column5: Projecting carbon and biodiversity outcomes through time Nature-based solutions and/or ecosystem-based approaches that provide climate change mitigation co-benefits should be selected on the basis of an assessment of the expected results, where such information is available. Benefits to biodiversity should be considered and estimated. Cost per ton of carbon dioxide equivalent should be considered and, together with resilience and ecological integrity considerations, may, for example, help countries to identify the types of conservation, restoration or management intervention most suitable for a given area. Urgent post-disaster responses may also provide opportunities to enhance benefits for biodiversity.

column3: Prioritize the prevention of further loss or degradation of natural ecosystem carbon stocks and, in a complementary and simultaneous manner where national circumstances permit, promote the restoration of degraded ecosystems and the recovery of their carbon stocks This principle is closely connected with the urgency principle and multiple benefit principles above. Emissions from the destruction of a natural ecosystem are near-instantaneous, while the carbon removals resulting from the full restoration of an equivalent area of the same ecosystem will typically take many years.

column5: Following the mitigation hierarchy The mitigation hierarchy should be considered when using nature-based solutions and/or ecosystem-based approaches that provide climate change mitigation co-benefits. Where there is a choice between reducing both negative impacts on biodiversity and emissions by preventing the loss or degradation of natural ecosystems (e.g. deforestation) and emissions removals by restoring natural ecosystems, and each option has similar mitigation benefits, the mitigation hierarchy should be followed where technically and economically feasible by prioritizing the conservation of existing carbon pools so as to avoid further negative impacts before restoring degraded ecosystems. Where comparable benefits can be achieved either by preventing loss or degradation or by restoring degraded ecosystems, avoidance of further biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation is the preferred approach. Only when prevention, reduction and restoration are insufficient or not technically feasible may compensation be considered as a last resort.
column6: 遵循減緩層級 在使用提供氣候變遷減緩共益之以自然為本的解決方案及／或以生態系為本的方法時，應考量減緩層級。若在「透過防止自然生態系喪失或退化（例如森林砍伐）以減少對生物多樣性之負面影響與排放」，與「透過復育自然生態系以移除排放」之間有所選擇，且兩項選項具相似的減緩效益時，在技術與經濟可行之情況下，應遵循減緩層級，優先保育現有碳庫，以便在復育退化生態系之前，避免進一步的負面影響。若無論是防止喪失或退化，或復育退化生態系，皆可達成相當之效益，則避免進一步的生物多樣性喪失與生態系退化為優先採行之方法。僅在預防、減少與復育不足或技術上不可行時，方可將補償視為最後手段。

column5: Promoting permanence Nature-based solutions and/or ecosystem-based approaches that provide climate change mitigation co-benefits should have long-lasting results. They should protect, maintain and restore biodiversity and ecological integrity (ecosystem condition, composition, structure and function). Actions should be designed to reduce the risk of reversals consistent with established environmental and social safeguard frameworks applicable to the relevant activity type (e.g. Cancun safeguard f),32 which typically means tackling the underlying drivers of ecosystem degradation and barriers to ecosystem restoration or sustainable management. Actions should be designed for climate and ecosystem resilience, prioritizing the use of local, climate-resilient native species in planting and restoration, and supporting the recovery of native flora and fauna and the ecological interactions that sustain long-term resilience. Monitoring systems should be able to assess any reversals, and carbon and biodiversity accounting or crediting systems should include buffers to cater for the remaining risk of reversals.

column3: Take a human rights-based approach, including by respecting and protecting the rights and roles of indigenous peoples and local communities, women and youth, who are crucial actors in both protecting and restoring biodiversity and in implementing climate action. Their traditional knowledge, priorities and needs should be taken into account for biodiversity and climate actions to be equitable, inclusive, effective and rights-based.
column4: 採取以人權為基礎之方法，包括尊重並保護原住民族與地方社區、女性及青年的權利與角色，其為保護與復育生物多樣性及執行氣候行動之關鍵行動者。應考量其傳統知識、優先事項與需求，以使生物多樣性與氣候行動具公平性、包容性、有效性並以權利為基礎。
column5: Promoting equitable outcomes Rights-based and gender-responsive considerations in the use of nature-based solutions and/or ecosystem-based approaches that provide climate change mitigation co-benefits should be designed and implemented with the full, effective, inclusive and gender-responsive participation and representation of indigenous peoples and local communities, women and youth, where applicable. Actions that present risks or imply potential risks of dispossession, undermine rights or fail to consider free, prior and informed consent or benefit-sharing, among others, should be identified, assessed and mitigated through robust grievance mechanisms, benefit-sharing arrangements and transparent monitoring, in line with host-country legal frameworks and applicable international standards. Actions with a direct or indirect impact on the rights of indigenous peoples and local communities should only be pursued with their free, prior and informed consent, subject to national legislation and consistent with international instruments. When risks to indigenous peoples and local communities, women or youth cannot be fully avoided, an accessible, culturally appropriate grievance and redress mechanism should be established and maintained to enable affected rights holders to raise concerns and obtain remedy throughout the project cycle.
column6: 促進公平成果 在使用提供氣候變遷減緩共益之以自然為本的解決方案及／或以生態系為本的方法時，以權利為基礎及具性別回應之考量，應在適用情況下，在原住民族與地方社區、女性及青年充分、有效、包容且具性別回應之參與及代表下設計與執行。凡存在或隱含剝奪、損害權利，或未考量自由、事先及知情同意或利益分享等風險之行動，應依地主國法律架構及適用之國際標準，透過健全的申訴機制、利益分享安排及透明監測加以識別、評估與減緩。對原住民族與地方社區之權利有直接或間接影響之行動，僅應在取得其自由、事先及知情同意，並符合國家立法與國際文書之情況下進行。當無法完全避免對原住民族與地方社區、女性或青年之風險時，應建立並維持可及且符合文化適切性之申訴與補救機制，使受影響之權利持有者能在整個專案週期中提出關切並獲得補救。
